island-biogeography.def: The study of how many species live on islands and why. Larger islands and islands closer to a source of colonists hold more species. The ideas also apply to habitat islands such as lakes, mountaintops and forest fragments.

habitat-fragmentation.def: The breaking of a large, continuous habitat into smaller patches separated by roads, farms, towns or other land its species cannot use. The patches act like islands, and small, isolated patches tend to lose species.
